questions.q: What is the central purpose of economic activity?
options: To make as much money as possible
To produce goods and services that satisfy needs and wants
To collect taxes for the government
questions.why: Economic activity exists to produce goods and services that satisfy people's needs and wants. Profit, jobs and taxes follow from it.

questions.q: A car maker decides to replace some workers on its production line with robots. Which key economic question is it answering?
questions.why: Choosing between workers and robots is a choice of method: how to produce.

questions.q: Match each decision to the key economic question it answers.
pairs: Building more hospitals instead of more roads
Using robots instead of workers on a car line
Making prescriptions free for everyone over 60
questions.why: What = which goods; how = which method and resources; who = who gets the output.

questions.q: Economists assume that people's wants are limited: once they have enough, they stop wanting more.
questions.why: Economists treat wants as unlimited: when one want is met, people find another. That is why resources are scarce.

questions.q: Which of these is a service rather than a good?
questions.why: A train journey is something done for you, not a physical product you keep.

questions.q: Explain the difference between a need and a want, with an example of each.

ideas.label: A need is essential for survival, e.g. food, water, shelter
A want is desirable but not essential, e.g. a phone or holiday

questions.model: A need is something essential for survival, such as food or shelter. A want is something we would like but could live without, such as a new phone.
questions.why: Needs are essentials for survival; wants are things we desire beyond that, and they are unlimited.

tests.answer: A need is something you must have to survive like water. A want is something you would like but could live without like a holiday.
A need is something like food that you need to survive.
They are basically the same thing.

questions.q: Match each resource to its factor of production.
pairs: A field used to grow wheat
Setting up a new business and risking your savings
questions.why: Natural resources are land, human effort is labour, man-made tools are capital, and organising plus risk-taking is enterprise.

questions.q: What is the reward to enterprise?
questions.why: Land earns rent, labour earns wages, capital earns interest, and enterprise earns profit as the reward for taking risk.

questions.q: Money saved in a firm's bank account counts as capital as a factor of production.
questions.why: Capital means man-made goods used in production, like machines and buildings. Money can buy capital but does not produce anything itself.

questions.q: Which of these is a capital good?
options: A tractor used on a farm
A pair of trainers bought by a student
questions.why: The tractor is used to produce other goods (crops). The others are consumer goods used up by households.

questions.q: Which of these is a non-renewable resource?
questions.why: Natural gas is used up and not replaced. Fish and timber are renewable if they are not used faster than they recover.

questions.q: What makes enterprise different from labour?
options: Enterprise is always done by a large company
Enterprise means organising the other factors and taking the risk of failure
Enterprise is only found in manufacturing
questions.why: An entrepreneur brings land, labour and capital together and bears the risk. Profit rewards that risk.

questions.topic: the environment is a scarce resource
questions.q: Explain why the environment is described as a scarce resource.

ideas.label: It is limited or can be used up or damaged (e.g. pollution, finite oil, over-fishing)
It has alternative uses, so using it one way has an opportunity cost

questions.model: The environment is limited: oil runs out, forests can be cut down faster than they grow, and pollution damages air and rivers. Because it has alternative uses, using it one way (for example, a river to carry waste) means giving up another use (fishing or drinking water), so it has an opportunity cost.
questions.why: Scarce means limited relative to the uses people want, so using it has an opportunity cost.

tests.answer: Because resources like oil are finite and will run out, and if a river is used to dump waste it cannot also be used for fishing, so there is an opportunity cost.
Because it is important to look after the planet.
